Alex: weird edge-case in the onboarding Retrofit sample: when we enable HTTP/2 multiplexing on emulator API 34, auth retries sometimes replay with a stale Authorization header and the Authenticator gets invoked again. Seems tied to when calls are enqueued concurrently from a coroutine Flow. Repro + notes below.

Priya: hmm. paste minimal client + logs?

Alex: client: ```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider)) // attaches header lazily? but ours captured value earlier
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator(tokenStore))
  .build()
```
logs: ```
I/OkHttp: stream 17 -> request /v1/items (Authorization: Bearer old)
W/OkHttp: response 401 for stream 17
I/Authenticator: refresh start id=aa1
I/Authenticator: refresh done id=aa1 new=eyJ.new
I/OkHttp: stream 18 -> request /v1/items (Authorization: Bearer old)
I/Authenticator: refresh start id=aa1 (duplicate)
```
Notice stream 18 is a concurrent call started by a Flow collector that read the token before the authenticator updated tokenStore. HTTP/2 multiplexing keeps multiple streams on the same connection and the timing makes the interceptor attach the old token.

Ben: afaik this is a variant of the interceptor vs authenticator ordering + stale-read problem, but the twist is the call factory / retrofit Call object capturing header at call creation time vs send time. If your AuthInterceptor does something like `val token = tokenProvider.get()` when the Call is created (or when Request.Builder is cloned earlier), you can end up with the old value.

Priya: right. two complementary fixes we used: 1) make the AuthInterceptor lazily evaluate the token _at send time_ instead of when the Request was originally created; 2) ensure tokenStore update happens-before other threads read it using a CompletableDeferred/MutableStateFlow so waiting coroutines can observe the new token and re-issue their requests. Example lazy approach: ```kotlin
class LazyAuthInterceptor(private val tokenProvider: () -> String?) : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val request = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", tokenProvider() ?: "")
      .build()
    return chain.proceed(request)
  }
}
```
This guarantees the provider lambda runs right before the request is executed.

Ben: for flows where multiple collectors call into Retrofit at the same time, we added a small in-memory broadcaster that the authenticator completes when refresh finishes. Callers who see 401 can wait on that broadcaster for a short timeout and then retry with the new token instead of blindly firing a new refresh. Eg: `synchronizedRefresh`: when first refresh starts, it sets a CompletableDeferred, other 401 handlers `await()` the same deferred rather than initiating refresh.

Alex: we also discovered a subtlety: Retrofit's `CallAdapter` for coroutines can create the underlying Call object early; ensure that headers are not baked into the Call at creation. Our fix: move Authorization header stamping into an interceptor (lazy) rather than into a custom `RequestFactory` that ran earlier.

Priya: additional mitigations: disable OkHttp connection-level automatic retry for auth-sensitive clients (`retryOnConnectionFailure(false)`), and for uploads/streaming bodies avoid automatic retries because bodies may be non-repeatable. Also, expose a small SDK helper `OkHttpClients.authSafe(tokenProvider)` to configure safe defaults (lazy auth interceptor, retryOnConnectionFailure(false), short call timeout, and a single-thread refresh coordinator).

Alex: I've pushed a draft PR `devex/http2-auth-lazy-provider` that: 1) replaces current interceptor with LazyAuthInterceptor; 2) adds a synchronized refresh coordinator using CompletableDeferred; 3) adds a small e2e test that spins up two concurrent Flow collectors emitting calls that provoke 401s. CI link: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/2788

Ben: follow-ups: - Add a note in the SDK docs about `Call` creation vs send time and recommend lazy header providers. - Add a sample for using MutableStateFlow/SharedFlow to broadcast token changes in apps that use coroutines. - Consider adding a helper `AuthRefreshCoordinator` in the SDK so apps don't reimplement deferred/sync logic.

Alex: opening tickets for docs + coordinator RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
